newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks leap ahead in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks leap ahead in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks absorbed overnight weaknesses from London then quickly leaped ahead on Wednesday morning on the back of positive interest rate and inflation news, brokers said.
"The outlook is no interest rate hikes in Hong Kong and likely decreases in China in the coming month or so," said one broker with an international house.
The Hang Seng Index put on 100 points to trade at 11,646.00 after 30 minutes of trade on Wedesday morning after a quick 34-point dip at the open.
Turnover was a respectable at nearly HK$1 billion.

The Wall Street Dow dropped 21 points after the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee decided on Tuesday not to raise U.S. interest rates. The Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London slipped 52 points overnight.
Brokers in Hong Kong, however, were taking a more bullish look at the market's near and longer term outlook.
"With no inflation or currency problems, Hong Kong is the best regional market (in Asia)," the international broker added.
Hong Kong's consumer price index for the month of August, released on Tuesday, showed a 4.9 percent rise in prices, the smallest gain in the index in nine years.
The commercial and industrial sector, followed by property stocks, led the rebound on Wednesday morning.

Red chip hong CITIC Pacific added HK$0.50 to HK$34.80 in early trading. Swire Pacific gained HK$0.25 to HK$68.25. The company recently announced it would be raising the sales prices of residential units in the second phase of its Island Place.
Hutchison inched up HK$0.25 to HK$50.25. Brokers expressed mixed views on the outlook for its London listed telecom subsidiary Orange Plc.

In the property sector, Sun Hung Kai Properties put on HK$1.00. Cheung Kong rose HK$56.50. The latter is still trending below its long-term resistance level of HK$57.25, a level that the share has tested seven times in the past eight months and failed to break through.
HSBC was unchanged at HK$141.50 in early trading, while Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.25 to HK$79.00.

Hopewell Holdings put on HK$0.025 to HK$4.25 in early trading. A local financial paper said the company would make an announcement on the sale of shares in Hopewell subsidiary Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA) next week.
